thirtyTwoBitSupportRationale: minSdk 26 still admits 32-bit-only Android 8 and 9 devices. Per-ABI splits cut the download for everyone without cutting those devices off, so 32-bit ships and is declared rather than being quietly present under a 64-bit-only claim. Dropping armeabi-v7a and x86 is a separate user-facing decision.

abiSplitEvidence.note: Per-ABI splits cut the download from 199 MB to 60 MB on the architecture every modern phone uses. That is still above IzzyOnDroid's 30 MB per-APK ceiling. The FFmpeg and Python payload remains because yt-dlp extraction, video crop, and codec fallbacks still use it. The Media3 sound-editor migration does not make the artifact eligible by itself.

mediaStackMigrationEvidence.implementation: Media3 Transformer now owns clipping, PCM fades, pitch-preserving speed, M4A, WAV, and device-supported OGG or Opus exports. FFmpeg only encodes codecs without a platform encoder and handles unsupported lossless packet copies.

tests.wavTrimFade: A one-second 8 kHz PCM fixture is trimmed to 600 ms, given exact 200 ms linear fades, and compared sample for sample against 4,800 expected PCM values.
tests.wavSpeed: A one-second 440 Hz PCM fixture exports at 2x in 490 to 510 ms while the detected pitch remains between 420 and 460 Hz.
tests.aacConvert: A one-second WAV fixture exports as audio/mp4a-latm at 192 kbps within a 975 to 1,025 ms duration window.

mediaStackMigrationEvidence.artifactBuild: The final signed public artifacts were rebuilt with optional provider BuildConfig defaults blank, then scanned against the workstation values before measurement.
mediaStackMigrationEvidence.sizeFinding: The native payload remains, so each FOSS split grew by 152,465 bytes and each full split grew by 156,597 to 156,601 bytes for this delivery.

legacyPackagingDecision.reason: youtubedl-android still expands zipped FFmpeg and Python payloads at runtime for stream extraction, video crop, and final codec fallbacks.

operations: M4A final encoding only if the device AAC encoder is unavailable
OGG final encoding only if the device Vorbis encoder is unavailable
Opus final encoding on Android 8 and 9 or when the device Opus encoder is unavailable
Lossless stream-copy cuts for MP3, FLAC, or source and container pairs Media3 cannot remux
YouTube stream extraction and segmented download merging

mediaStackMigrationEvidence.videoCropStatus: Video crop is the last direct video-editing consumer, but codec fallbacks and yt-dlp also remain.

nestedArchiveAlignmentExceptions.reason: Prebuilt libwebp object inside the published io.github.junkfood02.youtubedl-android:ffmpeg:0.18.1 AAR. yt-dlp extracts the archive at runtime and the FFmpeg binary dlopens what it needs, so the system loader never maps this ELF from the APK. It cannot be rebuilt here: the bytes ship inside a third-party artifact. Recorded rather than skipped so a new under-aligned payload still fails the gate.

nestedArchiveEvidence.note: The gate used to record lib/<abi>/*.zip.so as skipped, so roughly 250 shipped 64-bit ELFs per ABI were never measured. It now reads inside those archives. Measured against APKs assembled from the exact io.github.junkfood02.youtubedl-android 0.18.1 ffmpeg and library AAR payloads, because no release APK could be built on this host.
nestedArchiveEvidence.finding: Five libwebp objects inside libffmpeg.zip.so carry p_align 4096 on arm64-v8a and x86_64; every other 64-bit LOAD segment in both nested payloads is 16384. libpython.zip.so is fully compliant on both 64-bit ABIs. 32-bit ABIs are 4096 throughout, which carries no 16 KB obligation. The five are recorded in nestedArchiveAlignmentExceptions and the gate fails if a sixth appears or if a listed one stops being observed.
